tagline: One of three sisters, and all three go by Twisted.
intro: Out of Camp Wood, RM 337 crosses Camp Wood Creek twice and then takes to sharp curves, up and down steep hills, before it straightens out and runs into Leakey. Past the Frio River it runs through hilly country for several miles more and reaches the Sabinal River at Vanderpool.

The road is known for its hairpin switchbacks, and with RM 335 and RM 336 it makes up the loop called the Twisted Sisters. It began in 1945 as a farm road between Camp Wood and Leakey and was renamed a ranch road eleven years later.

moments.title: Leakey
moments.text: John Leakey settled by a spring on the Frio in 1856, and the place made shingles and lumber from cypress and cedar until ranching and Angora goats took over.

moments.title: Lost Maples State Natural Area
moments.text: Five miles north of Vanderpool, bigtooth maples thought to be left over from the cooler, wetter climate of the last glacial period color the Sabinal canyon in the fall.
